passage.title: Reading Part 2 - Test 04
passage.text:
Sleep is one of the most important biological processes in human life, yet many people fail to get enough of it. Scientists have spent decades studying sleep to understand why we need it and what happens when we don't get enough. Research has shown that sleep is not simply a passive state of rest but an active process during which the brain and body perform crucial maintenance and repair work.

During sleep, the brain goes through several distinct stages, each serving different functions. The first stage is light sleep, a transition period between wakefulness and sleep. This is followed by deeper stages of sleep where heart rate slows, body temperature drops, and the body begins repair processes. The most fascinating stage is REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep, during which most dreaming occurs. During REM sleep, the brain is highly active, processing memories and emotions from the day. Scientists believe that this stage is essential for learning and emotional regulation.

The consequences of sleep deprivation are serious and well-documented. People who consistently fail to get adequate sleep—typically 7-9 hours for adults—experience impaired cognitive function, including problems with memory, attention, and decision-making. Chronic sleep loss has also been linked to numerous health problems, such as obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and weakened immune function. Furthermore, lack of sleep can significantly affect mood, leading to irritability, anxiety, and depression.

Despite understanding the importance of sleep, modern society often treats it as a luxury rather than a necessity. The prevalence of electronic devices, irregular work schedules, and high-stress lifestyles all contribute to widespread sleep problems. However, experts emphasize that prioritizing sleep is one of the most important things people can do for their health. Establishing regular sleep schedules, creating comfortable sleep environments, and limiting screen time before bed are simple but effective strategies for improving sleep quality.
